risk_if_not_implemented: Without Data Quality Operations, inaccurate, stale, corrupted or manipulated data may drive flawed decisions and control failures. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Unauthorized Retention / Inability to Dispose of Data (R-AM-3), Loss of Data Integrity (R-IP-3), and most likely increases susceptibility to Human Error (MT-9), Data Quality Degradation / Data Poisoning (MT-12).

compensating_control_1.name: Sensitive / Regulated Data Governance
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate data governance so that sensitive and/or regulated data is effectively managed and maintained in accordance with applicable statutory, regulatory and contractual obligations.
compensating_control_1.justification: Sensitive / Regulated Data Governance (DCH-03) provides policy-level governance that compensates for the absence of Data Quality Operations (DCH-33) by establishing documented expectations, accountability structures, and organizational guardrails. Given the data-handling focus of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Data Quality Management
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to manage the quality, utility, objectivity, integrity and impact determination and de-identification of sensitive and/or regulated data across the information lifecycle.
compensating_control_2.justification: Data Quality Management (DCH-33.2) provides overlapping security capability that compensates for the absence of Data Quality Operations (DCH-33) by addressing related risk objectives through an alternative control mechanism aligned with Data applicability. Given the data-handling focus of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
